What if a political party's representatives decisions could be influenced and controlled by public voting. A technocracy, within a modern democracy. For example, a petition may be proposed, voted upon by members, validated through social security numbers/ whatever. Of course it may be controlled and manipulated as with anything over the course of time, but it seems more "representative" than anything we have now. The current level of political apathy seems almost tangible, and more involvement and discourse is required if the current system is to have any validity. Of course you will always have citizens heavily influenced by media and cultural prejudice, but the current system values an idea by the value of money behind it; it seems if not inevitable to be certainly achievable, and does not require a revolution.
True democracy. Technocracy. Is it feasible?

It's absolutely possible.

The immediate fear is like you mention - that people are very susceptible to outside influences. However, our elected representatives of today are more of an example of this phenomena than an exception so I think this concern is just disingenuous. The reality is there are many things we could do to vastly improve our political system. Our voting system itself, first-past-the-post, is completely broken. Replacing that with a simple proportional based voting system (if you get 10% of the votes, you get at least 10% of the seats and not 0% or 100%) would immediately get rid of gerrymandering, two party domination, and representatives who can't actually stand for anything.

Representatives who can't actually stand for anything? Think about the fact that a republican representative is somehow supposed to simultaneously represent neocons, small government supporters, libertarians, religious extremists, and many more segments. These groups are in many cases in direct conflict on their fundamental beliefs. Therefore the representatives are unable to take any meaningful stand without isolating large chunks of their constituency. The same is true of the liberal side of things. I think much of the left despise our totalitarian segments, the "social justice" types in particular, that would happily sacrifice free speech and expression -tenants absolutely fundamental to liberalism- to push their agenda. But you'll never hear a single left leaning politician start speaking out against these people. They show up to the polls reliably and so even if their views go against everything we ought stand for, we're forced to accept them thanks to first-past-the-post.

And the giant pink elephant in the room? Corporate influence? Well first-past-the-post is an all or nothing game. That means you get the majority of the vote and get all the seats, or you get nothing. That means big dollar campaign costs. And where does that money come from? This isn't a partisan issue either. Republicans get more flack for selling out to corporations. On the other hand, who appointed a lifetime telecom lobbyist to the FCC? Who appointed a Monsanto VP to deputy commission of foods at the FDA? Oh, and something most people are completely unaware of. What party does Tom Wheeler caucus with?

This is the reason the parties oppose each other on "safe" issues - abortion rights, gun rights, should we give this social program 17% funding or 21% funding, and so forth. They're inoffensive battle lines that let us get our big groups together unified in little more than our dislike for the other group. However, the players in control of this system have learned to love it and as the people in power, people under no constitutional obligations to the people they're supposed to represent, they can do whatever they want. And changing our political system would likely mean these people, the people who now get to pull the strings of fate for arguably the most influential country in the world, would end up unemployed en masse. I somehow don't think they'll just come along with the idea.

I'm imagining a society such as Australia. To be clear, I mean a party adopting this practice, not a system. Yes, corporate influence will do their best to maintain the status quo, yet to assume that WE do not possess any ability to spread an idea to others is to submit all potential for change, and these words means nothing.If we are able to simply inject this into the public imagination as a possibility, enough people may subscribe to the idea. It may take a generation, but the youth are more interconnected and susceptible to new ideas than ever before. This is an idea that is needed more than any other.

How hard would it be to create an official party and a website, and the promise of acting in the public interest; with an authoritative referendum backing up every action? Surely this would command more authority than opponents. It may even be used against our best interest, but it seems preferable in a strange way.

It does not have to happen in America, but any nation, to prove that there are possible alternatives to representative democracy and dictatorships. The idea that this is best because everything else we have tried has seemed to fail is a flawed logic, and our system as it stands may be so devoid of reason that it will destroy the world.

We always think that "they" are in control. And they are in a way. But to submit to this control, illusionary or real, is to surrender. Change is possible.

There are partial implementations of this idea. Here's a nice article on Switzerland's public democracy system.

I think the problem is that the word democracy, or even a democratic republic, is no longer indicative. You seem to have been alluding to the famous quote that "Democracy is the worst system, except all the others that we've tried." but that quote is no longer particularly meaningful. Switzerland is also a democractic republic, but I think you can see that they share very little in common with the authoritarian level of power granted to the US government. If we look at the US government itself as a black box, their power is completely unchecked.

There are various imperfect renditions of such an idea; such as the white-house petitions; but I'm imagining a populist opposition that is decided upon popular opinion. How could anyone oppose a party that supports what most people favour. I know this is a dangerous idea taken to extremes, I dare think of the vile thoughts that are popularly held under the surface of reason.

I simply think hat to have a hundred or so people making choices in the"best interest" of others is just as preposterous as having one or three. A rational system that was not devoted to self perpetuation would have hundreds if not millions of politically active individuals. A party or system that utilizes such a technocratic basis would provide an avenue for political involvement that is no longer founded upon the illusion that the decision of any individual is inherently better; that the people at the top are often just as ignorant and uninformed than the people at the bottom, if not more so.

The biggest problem is the current system in place. Very few people in the current government want to see it fundamentally change. Why? They were elected / appointed / hired under the current system. If we change that system they may lose their job / power / influence. Much better to keep the status quo and act like everything is normal.

That said, it would be great if there was a way to implement this that would be immune to manipulation. Take the other voting site as an example. Look how well that worked out. Power hungry mods, censorship, manipulation of information....how would it work on a nationwide scale? I just don't know, but anything is better than where we are headed.

I believe that it can operate within the "system" itself, whilst I certainly believe it needs changes. But I also believe that "people power" is a very real force. Look at kickstarter. There should be some form of communication in the public about proposed changes, and the people who are most affected are likely to voice their concerns. Think about gay marriage. If it was of concern, you would likely have input, whilst if you were simply homophobic, i doubt you would even be aware. Not that it even matters. Computers will own the world irregardless, ideally before we lay waste to the world and induce a fiery dystopia. It would be nice to sort our shit out before we all die

I see what you are getting at, but that system within the system will destroy or radically transform the parent system. So those in the parent system will have a vested interest in insuring they are not made obsolete, exposed or removed. That is the problem. Not saying it can't be done, just that I don't see how it can be.

Kickstarter etc are great examples, but they do not threaten anyone. Now a kickstarter type deal to put some very independent candidate in place would be an interesting first step. But that was basically done with Ron Paul and we all know how that ended.

I'm not against you @naked_donkey. Just trying to add some salt to the discussion to generate questions and ideas.

"just that I don't see how it can be" - It is a perfectly rational response; but if we assume that everything and every antiestablishment idea is controlled and censored, then what is the point in any action at all. They use fear and control upon all of us- but people are still individuals with the power to listen and to make decisions. How often have you heard the word technocracy in the public media? I believe that ideas, if they hold value, may spread.

How did communism result in Russia and other nations? Sure there was revolutions, repression and so on, but it was an idea that spread amongst intellectuals well before it was realized. If we simply talked, and communicated our ideals of what was to be done, on the internet, through media and discourse, it may be realized as a potential alternative to what is in place. But if we refuse to believe in possibilities due to the existence of an elite assuming control, should that not increase our drive for change? Even if all is doomed to fail,at least we will be able to say we tried.

The current intellectual contagion is of the importance of the self over all others; a perpetual drive to entropy that is to be capitalised upon rather than changed. We think in terms of our own values, unable to visualize the billions of others around us, and the earth in its entirety; devoid of responsibility for our actions, and rewarding exploitation of others.

If we wanted to create a new reality, we must first create a language and an understanding to be spread.

How was communism and feminism created? it was not an individual. It was a collective way of thought. If we are to enact change, we must not only change the way we think, but change others, and genuinely care about issues that we value. Language is its own reality.
